title: UI: prompt and tool forms render no send button (dataset assignment throws)
description: schema_form.js has its own el() helper that lacks the 'dataset' branch app.js's el() has. It falls through to `k in node` -> `node.dataset = {...}`, and dataset is a readonly WebIDL attribute, so in a module (strict mode) the assignment throws TypeError. renderField() and buildPromptForm() both pass dataset, so buildForm/buildPromptForm throw, renderToolDetail/renderPromptDetail abort, and the detail panel shows the heading with no form and no send button. Templates are unaffected (they use app.js's el).
acceptance_criteria: Opening a prompt (e.g. zoo-prompt-animal) or a tool with fields shows its form and its send button; data-field is set on each field so the variables column can fill it.
close_reason: el() in schema_form.js and render.js now handle dataset explicitly

title: A backend restart never told clients the catalogue changed

title: Three UI bugs only a browser found: painted gate, /ui base URL, endless retry
description: Found by driving the page in headless Chromium over CDP. (1) .gate sets display:grid, which outranks the UA stylesheet's [hidden]{display:none}, so the access-key overlay was painted permanently over a working page while el.hidden reported true -- every DOM assertion passed. Fixed with an explicit [hidden]{display:none!important}. (2) A document served at /ui has / as its base URL, so the browser resolved style.css to /style.css and 404'd: an unstyled page with no JS from a URL that answered 200. /ui now 308s to /ui/, preserving the query string. (3) A page on the gate reconnected forever, a 401 every few seconds; a socket that never connected now stops after three attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Gate is display:none when hidden; /ui 308s to /ui/ keeping ?key=; retries bounded. tests/test_webui.py covers the redirect.
close_reason: Closed

title: make run never started the daemon: cli.py had no __main__ guard
description: scripts/start-gateway.sh invokes 'python -m mcp_gateway.cli'. cli.py defined run() but had no 'if __name__ == "__main__"' guard, so the module imported, defined everything and exited 0 without binding anything. The Makefile prints the banner itself, so it looked exactly like a daemon that had started. The console script (mcp-gateway) calls run() through its entry point and was never affected, which is why every test and every hand-run missed it. Found while verifying 'make run-dev'.
acceptance_criteria: 'python -m mcp_gateway.cli --check' runs and exits 0 with the check report; tests/test_cli_paths.py asserts it.
close_reason: Closed

title: A vocabulary value cannot be put in an enum-constrained field
description:
Found by the new jsdom harness (python-mcp-gateway-6cm), which is the first thing able to reach it.

An enum select built by schema_form.js carries the choice's *index* as each option's value -- deliberately, so `{"enum": [0, 1, 3, 5]}` comes back as the number 3 rather than the string "3" (schema_form.js:355). `putValue` in app.js matches the value it is given against `option.value`, so for any such field the match is index-against-value and always fails: clicking 'asia' in the variables column reports 'asia is not one of the choices this field offers', about a field that offers exactly that.

Reachable whenever a tool or prompt argument has an `enum` in its schema and the same server publishes a vocabulary for that argument's name -- which is the ordinary case for a server that constrains its inputs.
acceptance_criteria: A pick lands in an enum select whose schema names it, the collected value keeps its JSON type (a number stays a number), and a value the field genuinely does not offer still reports so. Covered in tests/ui/.
close_reason: putValue now matches an option on either spelling; schema_form.js carries the choice's own value on option.dataset.value beside the index that collect() needs. Covered in tests/ui/choices.test.mjs.

title: Decide whether the UI JS gets a real test harness (jsdom)
description:
The six files under src/mcp_gateway/ui/ are covered by `node --check` and nothing else.
webui.md and tests/test_webui.py state that position deliberately: "this project has no
Node toolchain and is not acquiring one to run a parser", and what the modules *do* is
verified by eye through `make run-dev`. This issue exists to decide whether the cascade
work changed that calculation, not to assume it did.

The evidence that it might. Two bugs reached a commit in one sitting, both in code no
Python test can reach:

  1. A cascade child inherited its parent's variable, so the grandchild's URI was built by
     writing the country into the continent's segment -- `zoo://continents/congo/countries//animals`.
     Caught before committing, by running the resolver's real source against stub state.
  2. Opening a template after making the picks left every field empty: the column applied
     only `many` picks when a form opened, which was correct until the cascade made
     picking-before-opening the normal order. This one SHIPPED, in 4c8d117, and was found
     by the user in the browser.

Both were logic, not syntax, and both were cheap to catch once there was a DOM to run
against -- jsdom happened to resolve from a global install on this machine, and the fill
path (renderResourceDetail -> applyPicks -> controlFor -> putValue) ran in about thirty
lines of harness.
design:
The shape that fits what already exists, if this is adopted:

- A dev-only dependency. jsdom, in an optional extra or a tests/ui/package.json, NOT a
  runtime one -- the daemon still ships with no Node anything, and the CSP argument in
  webui.md is untouched.
- Driven from pytest, the way tests/test_webui.py::test_the_modules_parse already drives
  `node --check`: skipped when node or jsdom is absent, so a checkout without them stays
  green. That keeps one test command and avoids a second CI toolchain.
- Worth covering, in order of what has actually broken: the variables column's resolver
  (root pairing and dedupe, narrows expansion, pending groups, pick pruning when an
  upstream changes or a vocabulary closes) and the fill path in both directions (a pick
  clicked into an open form, and a form opened onto picks already made).
- Not worth covering: rendering detail, styling, the sockets. The value is in the pure-ish
  logic that the DOM merely hosts.

The honest cost, which is the reason this is a decision and not a task: it reverses a
stated position, adds a second language's dependency to a repo that has none, and jsdom is
not a browser -- it has no layout, so `scrollIntoView` had to be polyfilled even in the
throwaway harness. A test that passes there can still be wrong in a browser.

The alternative is to leave it as it is and accept that UI regressions are found by eye.
That is defensible for a test bench whose whole job is to be looked at; it is less
defensible now that the column has state -- opened sets, chains, picks with lifetimes --
rather than being a renderer of listings.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded either way. If adopted: jsdom is a dev-only dependency, the suite runs from pytest and skips cleanly without node or jsdom, the resolver and both directions of the fill path are covered, and webui.md's 'no Python test can cover these' paragraph is rewritten to say what now does. If declined: webui.md says why, so the next person does not reopen it.
close_reason: Decided: adopted. jsdom as a dev-only dep in tests/ui/package.json, driven from tests/test_webui_js.py (skips without node or jsdom), 47 tests over the resolver and both directions of the fill path. webui.md now has a 'How the JavaScript is tested' section that states the reversal and its limits.

title: Variables column: two templates over one listing alias each other
description: vocabularyPairs() cuts a template at its first brace to find the listing it pairs with, so two templates sharing a fixed prefix both pair with the same listing URI. vocabularies and picks are keyed by that URI, so the two groups alias each other's cache and pick state. Keep exactly one pairing per listing URI: fewest variables, then shortest template, then lexicographic.
acceptance_criteria: a server publishing two templates over one listing shows one group, and its pick state is its own
close_reason: Cascade landed both ways: zoo publishes zoo://continents plus two listing templates chained by a 'narrows' key beside 'readOne', the Variables column resolves and prunes dependent groups, and completion/complete is forwarded end to end with context.arguments and offered as a datalist. vocabularyPairs() now keeps one pairing per listing URI, fixing the aliasing. tests/test_zoo_cascade.py and tests/test_completions.py cover both; 429 tests, lint and docs-check green.

title: Cascading vocabularies: continent -> country -> animal

acceptance_criteria: zoo publishes zoo://continents plus two listing templates; the Variables column shows dependent groups that stay pending until upstream is picked, re-read on change, and prune downstream picks; tests/test_zoo_cascade.py green
close_reason: Cascade landed both ways: zoo publishes zoo://continents plus two listing templates chained by a 'narrows' key beside 'readOne', the Variables column resolves and prunes dependent groups, and completion/complete is forwarded end to end with context.arguments and offered as a datalist. vocabularyPairs() now keeps one pairing per listing URI, fixing the aliasing. tests/test_zoo_cascade.py and tests/test_completions.py cover both; 429 tests, lint and docs-check green.

title: schema_form.js: a form generated from a tool's inputSchema
description: Pure functions build(schema) -> {fields, declined, reason} and collect(fields) -> args. Renders properties, required, type, title, description, default, enum (+enumNames/oneOf[].title), format, minimum/maximum/multipleOf, minLength/maxLength, pattern, items for arrays, nested objects two deep, and dependentRequired. Declines if/then/else, dependentSchemas, allOf and discriminated oneOf, stepping aside to a raw JSON box with a one-line reason. Three distinct states: properties with entries -> form; properties: {} -> 'takes no parameters'; no inputSchema -> raw box and no claim. Validation is a convenience, never a trust boundary: every form has a raw-JSON view of the wire payload and a send-anyway escape. Contract: python-acp docs/tool-schema-contract.md.
acceptance_criteria: Against the zoo: zoo-choices renders dropdowns, zoo-numbers bounded number inputs, zoo-empty says it takes no parameters, zoo-silent gives a raw box, and the four composition tools decline with a reason.
close_reason: Closed

close_reason: notifications.py (per-kind debounce, progress to the originating connection, message logged not relayed, resources/updated dropped), reverse passthrough with capability gating, cancellation propagation, multi-client capability union. 307 tests green. Found a real bug the tests were the only thing that could catch: a contextvars.ContextVar does NOT reach the backend's server-request handler, because mcp_stdio dispatches it from the read-loop task created in start() — a task copies its context at creation, so a value set by a later call is invisible. Origin is now tracked explicitly on the Backend, and two clients mid-call on one backend is an honest refusal rather than a coin flip. Also fixed a deadlock in the mock fixture: it polled for the client's answer inside its own stdin loop.

title: TLS (wss://) for non-loopback deployments
Restart backoff for a backend that crashes on every call
description: consecutive_failures is tracked; add exponential backoff so a crash-looping backend does not burn CPU.

title: Lazy backend spawn with idle TTL
description: Eager spawn was chosen for v1. A 20-backend daemon will want lazy spawn plus idle-TTL teardown.

title: resources/subscribe + resources/updated URI rewriting
description: Currently subscribe:false and updated notifications are dropped. Needs mcpgw:// rewriting on the updated notification path.

title: Authorization-header-only WS auth, retire ?key=
description: Query-param keys land in access logs. Move to Authorization: Bearer only once the bridge and UI both send headers.

title: Streamable-HTTP transport (bridge-free path for Claude Code)
description: Serve MCP streamable HTTP on the same port so clients can attach natively without mcp-gateway-connect.

title: Gateway admin UI
description: Web UI over the /admin WS path: config CRUD (admin.config.set), secret management (admin.secrets.set — /admin only, never /mcp), backend add/remove, live status and log streaming.

title: logging/setLevel forwarding to backends
completion/complete forwarding
description: Forward completion/complete to the backend that owns the ref, including context.arguments (the spec's cascade). Advertise the completions capability unconditionally and answer an empty values list for a backend that declares none. Zoo answers completions over the continent/country/animal data; the UI offers them as a datalist on template-variable and prompt-argument inputs.
close_reason: Cascade landed both ways: zoo publishes zoo://continents plus two listing templates chained by a 'narrows' key beside 'readOne', the Variables column resolves and prunes dependent groups, and completion/complete is forwarded end to end with context.arguments and offered as a datalist. vocabularyPairs() now keeps one pairing per listing URI, fixing the aliasing. tests/test_zoo_cascade.py and tests/test_completions.py cover both; 429 tests, lint and docs-check green.
